conclusions: At B05 G4, conventional Richards and Layer-ROM have identical event errors: 9 bottom-flux sign mismatches, 4 reversal-sequence mismatches and 1024-step reversal-timing error.
At B05 G6, conventional Richards and Layer-ROM again have identical event errors: 9 sign mismatches, 4 sequence mismatches and 1024-step timing error.
Therefore the persistent B05 reversal failure is not attributable to the reduced CURRENT_LAYER_FACE propagation/closure used by Layer-ROM.
G4→G6 materially improves all continuous same-partition Richards groundwater metrics, but provides zero improvement on the discrete event vector.

Reduced propagation/closure contributes modest additional continuous error because COR_G4 and COR_G6 are componentwise better than LR_G4 and LR_G6 on the continuous vector, but this does not explain the event failure.
The remaining B05 event defect is attributable to insufficient or misplaced vertical representation at G4/G6, or to a material-specific nonlinear response that those partitions cannot resolve.

decision.next_question: Does eight-state lower-focused G8 resolve the B05 event defect, and is lower-focused G8 better or worse than equal-dimension U8?
decision.rationale: This directly separates state-count/lower-zone support from placement mismatch before any new closure family or empirical repair.
